title: The Pendulum in International Affairs
summary:
This process boosted economic growth in the emerging nations where the work was done,
increased savings and competitiveness for manufacturers and importers, and
provided low-priced goods to consumers. As each country benefited from the growth of manufacturing, the supply of labor got tighter,
and workers became able to demand higher wages. Wages may have risen locally, but as a consequence, the search for low-margin, low-skill
work moved on to new low-cost venues.
